title: Porus Asks to Be Treated Like a King
text:
In 326 BC Alexander the Great crossed the Hydaspes River in the Punjab and met the army of the Indian king Porus. It was one of Alexander's hardest battles. Porus fought from a huge war elephant at the center of his line and kept fighting after his army had broken, though badly wounded.

Plutarch says historians agreed Porus was very tall, and that his elephant protected him through the battle, kneeling gently when he weakened. When Porus was finally brought before Alexander, the conqueror asked him how he wished to be treated. Porus answered: "As a king." Alexander asked whether he had nothing more to say. Porus replied that everything was contained in that word. Arrian, writing from earlier sources, gives the same exchange.

Alexander was impressed by his courage and dignity. He gave Porus back his kingdom to rule as his ally and added to it territory of neighboring peoples. Porus remained loyal to Alexander afterward.
lesson: Keep your dignity in defeat. People who keep their self-respect when they have lost tend to win the respect of the one who beat them.
source: Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander 5.19; Plutarch, Life of Alexander 60
